title: Conformance snapshot
description: How far a repository's tree is from its architecture manifest, as `architecture conformance --json` reports it. See https://dataquail.github.io/goodbones/architecture-rules/enforcement/conformance/.

path.description: The file the policy was read from — the root file, when split with `include`.

sha256.description: A hash of that file's bytes, so two snapshots can say whether the policy changed between them.

manifest.description: The policy this snapshot was taken against — the repository's own, or the one `--against` named.

ok.description: What `check` would exit with: true when no reportable violation, unresolved import, stale baseline entry or coverage shortfall exists.

allOf.description: The fraction the manifest's `limits.coverage` states for this family, when it states one.
The fraction the manifest's `limits.coverage` states for this family, when it states one.
The fraction the manifest's `limits.coverage` states for this family, when it states one.

The fraction the manifest's `limits.coverage` states for this family, when it states one.

coverage.description: Per family, how many walked files it reaches. Structure counts enumerated folders only.

folders.description: Folders every walked file of which is residue, each the topmost such folder.

residue.description: What the policy has nothing to say about. A file in an open folder under no allowlist is claimed, not policed, and counts.

allOf.description: Distinct entries the node wrote, `allow` and `external` together.

vacant.description: Nodes that state an import allowlist and select no walked file, in manifest order. Every allowance on one is unused by construction, so none is counted as slack; the node is a tier declared ahead of its first file, or a pattern that no longer matches. Residue is files no node reaches; this is nodes no file reaches.

fingerprint.description: kind|rule|file|subject — line-independent, so it survives edits to the file it names; the baseline's key.

ruleName.description: The manifest node path the rule was lowered from.

subject.description: The other end of the violated relationship — the resolved target, the restricted symbol, the missing sibling — or null when the file alone is the violation.

baselined.description: Carried by the baseline, so `check` does not fail on it.

route.description: For a graph `reach` violation: the files the origin reached the target through, origin first, target last.

violations.description: Every finding, baselined ones included, ordered so the ones cheapest to fix come first: by the height of the violated target in the import graph, leaves first.

unresolved.description: Imports the resolver could not turn into a file. Every rule about one enforces nothing.

stale.description: Baseline entries the code no longer produces.

baseline.description: The debt the policy is carrying. The ratchet: it may only shrink.

allOf.description: Strongly connected components of more than one file, or a file importing itself, anywhere in the walked graph — in a cycles rule's scope or not.

node.description: The manifest node that wrote the entry — or, when `fragment` is set, the `defs` fragment it was written in.

kind.description: `allow` is a path glob under `imports.allow`; `external` a package name under `imports.external`.

entry.description: The entry as written, after alias expansion.

fragment.description: Present when the entry arrived through `use`. The nodes that referenced the fragment wrote one word, so the entry is reported once, against the fragment, rather than once per node.

allOf.description: With `fragment`: how many non-vacant nodes were granted the entry through it. None of them uses it.

slack.description: Allowances no observed import uses, in manifest order, vacant nodes excluded. A manifest inferred from the tree has none on the day it is written; every entry here is permission nothing needs. An entry that arrived through `use` is reported once, against the fragment, and only when no node granted it uses it.

fragment.description: The `defs` fragment the entry was written in.

kind.description: `allow` is a path glob under `imports.allow`; `external` a package name under `imports.external`.

entry.description: The entry as written, after alias expansion.

allOf.description: Nodes granted the entry through the fragment that use it.
Non-vacant nodes granted the entry through the fragment.

concentration.description: Fragment entries used at some of the nodes granted them and not the rest. Not slack — the fragment's line is needed somewhere — but a per-file permission written as a many-node allowance, which is what an allowlist widened to make one build green looks like.

adoption.description: The tiers that said "not tightened yet", by name; `limits` caps how many may.
